subject: anatomy
title: Forearm, wrist and hand: anatomy essentials for exams

steps.tx: The **forearm** is split into flexor and extensor compartments by the interosseous membrane and the two bones. The flexor compartment has three layers and is supplied mainly by the median nerve, while the extensor compartment is supplied by the radial nerve. Know which nerve supplies which compartment.
steps.say: The forearm is split into flexor and extensor compartments by the interosseous membrane and the two bones. The flexor compartment has three layers and is supplied mainly by the median nerve. The extensor compartment is supplied by the radial nerve. Know which nerve supplies which compartment.

steps.tx: The **carpal tunnel** lies deep to the **flexor retinaculum**. The median nerve and the flexor tendons pass through it. Structures lying superficial to the retinaculum include the palmaris longus, the ulnar vessels and nerve, and palmar cutaneous branches. These are not at risk in carpal tunnel compression.
steps.say: The carpal tunnel lies deep to the flexor retinaculum. The median nerve and the flexor tendons pass through it. Structures superficial to the retinaculum include the palmaris longus, the ulnar vessels and nerve, and palmar cutaneous branches. These are not at risk in carpal tunnel compression.

steps.tx: **Guyon's canal** lies on the ulnar side of the wrist and transmits the ulnar nerve and ulnar artery. Its roof is the palmar carpal ligament and its floor is the flexor retinaculum. Handlebar injury from cycling can compress the nerve here, causing sensory loss on the ulnar side of the hand.
steps.say: Guyon's canal lies on the ulnar side of the wrist and transmits the ulnar nerve and ulnar artery. Its roof is the palmar carpal ligament and its floor is the flexor retinaculum. steps.tx: The **anatomical snuffbox** is a triangular depression on the radial side of the wrist. Its lateral border is formed by abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis. Its medial border is extensor pollicis longus. The floor is the scaphoid and trapezium, and the radial artery runs through it. Tenderness here suggests a **scaphoid fracture**.

steps.tx: The **palmar arches** supply the hand. The superficial arch is mainly a continuation of the ulnar artery and lies near the palmar aponeurosis. The deep arch is mainly a continuation of the radial artery and lies deeper, close to the bases of the metacarpals. The Allen test checks the patency of these connections before radial artery harvest.
steps.say: The palmar arches supply the hand. The superficial arch is mainly a continuation of the ulnar artery and lies near the palmar aponeurosis. The deep arch is mainly a continuation of the radial artery and lies deeper, close to the bases of the metacarpals. The Allen test checks the patency of these connections before radial artery harvest.

steps.tx: The **thenar muscles** are mainly supplied by the median nerve. Adductor pollicis is the exception and is supplied by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve. The hypothenar muscles are supplied by the ulnar nerve. Nearly all intrinsic hand muscles are ulnar, except the first and second lumbricals and the thenar muscles, which are median. The **lumbricals** flex the metacarpophalangeal joints and extend the interphalangeal joints.

steps.tx: Finally, the **radioulnar joints** allow forearm rotation. Supination and pronation occur at the proximal and distal radioulnar joints, not at the middle one. Pronator teres and pronator quadratus pronate, while supinator and biceps supinate. Fractures like the **Colles fracture** can disturb the distal radioulnar joint and the triangular fibrocartilage, so check forearm rotation after injury.
